title: Indeterminate form
text: Substitute $$x$$ with the value $$x$$ approaches to. If the function results in one of these indeterminate form: $$\frac{0}{0}$$, $$\frac{\infty}{\infty}$$ or $$\frac{-\infty}{\infty}$$, we apply L’Hôpital’s Rule.

title: Substitute the limit
text: As $$x$$ approaches $$0$$ from the right side of the $$y$$ axis, the graph of lnx approaches negative infinity and the graph of cotx approaches $$\infty$$. Therefore, $$\lim_{x\to0} \frac{lnx}{cotx}=\frac{-\infty}{\infty}$$.

title: Apply L’Hôpital’s Rule
text: Differentiate the denominator and the numerator separately: $$\lim_{x\to0} \frac{\frac{d}{dx} lnx}{\frac{d}{dx} cotx}$$

title: Find the derivative
text: What is the answer of the function after L’Hôpital’s Rule is applied?

subHints.title: Evaluate the limit
subHints.text: If we plug $$0$$ into $$x$$ in the denominator at this point, the first term is approaching zero meanwhile the second term is approaching a very large number. The expression would be written as: $$\frac{1}{0} \left(-\infty\right)$$. In such a case, we can not make any conclusion yet.

title: Rearrange the expression
text: In order to make the expression easier to apply the L’Hôpital’s Rule a second time, we need to rearrange the expression using the definition of cscx. We then apply the apply L’Hôpital’s Rule and Evaluate the limit

title: Apply L’Hôpital’s Rule again
text: Rewrite $$\frac{1}{-\left(x {\operatorname{csc}\left(x\right)}^2\right)}$$ as $$\frac{sin^2\left(x\right)}{\left(-x\right)}$$. Differentiate the denominator and the numerator separately: $$\lim_{x\to0} \frac{\frac{d}{dx} sin^2\left(x\right)}{\frac{d}{dx} \left(-x\right)}$$

title: Apply L’Hôpital’s Rule again
text: What is the answer of the function after the L’Hôpital’s Rule and the Chain Rule are applied?

subHints.title: Apply Chain Rule
subHints.text: By the Chain Rule, the derivative of $$sin^2\left(x\right)$$ is $$2sinx cosx$$.
